jvmParams.enabled.title: Enable JVM Default Parameters
jvmParams.enabled.description: Master switch. When off, nothing is written: no .openidea/run.toml entry, no configuration file is patched.

jvmParams.vmOptions.title: VM options
jvmParams.vmOptions.description: The JVM options appended to every launch configuration of the project, on one line. Quotes are allowed for values with spaces. Example: -Xmx2g -Xms512m -XX:+UseG1GC -Dfile.encoding=UTF-8

jvmParams.programArgs.title: Program arguments
jvmParams.programArgs.description: The application arguments appended to every launch configuration, on one line. Leave empty to only inject JVM options. Example: --server.port=8081 --spring.profiles.active=dev

jvmParams.springProfiles.title: Spring profiles
jvmParams.springProfiles.description: Comma separated profiles, appended as --spring.profiles.active=… after the main class of every saved configuration.

jvmParams.pinToProject.title: Pin these values to this project
jvmParams.pinToProject.description: On by default. Apply writes the values into this project's .openidea/settings.toml, which wins over the global values: changing the global setting afterwards no longer changes this project. The plugin's settings page always opens in the Global scope (the IDE offers no way for a plugin to choose), so this is what keeps a project safe. Turn it off to follow the global values again.

jvmParams.mode.title: Merge mode
jvmParams.mode.description: append keeps every value a configuration already sets and only fills the gaps; override replaces the value of a JVM switch the configuration already sets. Both keep the order the configuration already has, and both are idempotent.
